incident.observed_boundary: After the required Git-credential prompt was visibly present and explicit No was accepted, GitHub CLI displayed the one-time device code. Core incorrectly requested a screenshot of that screen even though the frozen contract prohibited exposing the code to Core/chat.

problem.security_effect: A screenshot requested at the device-code display boundary can transmit the one-time code into chat and violates the secrecy boundary before device authorization.
problem.design_error: The operator contract prohibited sharing the code but did not freeze a nonsecret progress-reporting protocol for the exact device-code display boundary, allowing Core to request contradictory visual evidence.

remediation_scope.principle: At the one-time device-code boundary, progress must be reported without images or code-bearing text. Core must never request evidence that can contain the device code.

device_code_display_boundary: When the GitHub CLI one-time device code becomes visible, do NOT send a screenshot, photo, screen recording, OCR output, copied terminal text, transcription, or the code itself to Core/chat.
Core MUST NOT request a screenshot, photo, copied terminal output, or any visual/text evidence of the device-code screen.
Owner reports only the fixed nonsecret acknowledgement `DEVICE_CODE_DISPLAYED_NO_CODE_SHARED`. No device-code characters may accompany that acknowledgement.
Only after a fresh authority/binding check may Core instruct the single reviewed Enter action that advances GH_BROWSER=/bin/true into the device-flow wait/poll state.
The device code may be used only locally between the dedicated Codespace terminal and first-party GitHub device-authorization UI. It must not be relayed through Core/chat.

If the one-time code is transmitted to Core/chat or any unreviewed destination, STOP before device authorization when still possible, delete the Codespace, close the receipt as consumed/nonreusable, and return for review. No retry in that session.
first_party_device_authorization_boundar: After Enter, complete only the first-party GitHub device-authorization flow.

Do not send screenshots from the device-authorization boundary to Core. Owner reports only the fixed nonsecret acknowledgement `GITHUB_DEVICE_CONNECTED_NO_CODE_SHARED` after GitHub confirms the device is connected.
If first-party GitHub does not confirm connection, or any unexpected prompt/page/redirect occurs, STOP and return to Core under the existing no-retry failure contract.
returned_codespace_boundary: After returning to the same dedicated Codespace, do not send a terminal screenshot while the one-time code is visible anywhere in the captured viewport.

Core does not require screenshot proof of OAuth return. Operator may report only the reviewed nonsecret markers/status in text; the subsequent post-OAuth clean-shell/trusted-Python/Step2.6 gates remain the enforcement mechanism.
A later screenshot may be used only if the Owner first visually confirms that the one-time device code is not visible in the captured viewport. If uncertain, use text-only reporting.
exact_v10_override.downstream_chain: v4/v8 post-OAuth clean-shell reentry, trusted-Python gate, Step 2.6 rehydrate/reverify, canonical exact effective-scope gate, and NONMUTATING Step 3 remain unchanged.

consolidated_review_unit.unit: OAuth command + mandatory Git-credential prompt presence + explicit No + device-code secrecy/nonvisual acknowledgement + Enter/device-flow transition + first-party GitHub authorization + nonvisual connection acknowledgement + returned-shell boundary + post-OAuth clean shell + trusted Python + Step 2.6 + exact effective scopes + nonmutating Step 3
consolidated_review_unit.review_goal: Sweep the complete interactive OAuth/device-flow and downstream diagnostic chain for contradictory evidence requests or any other statically discoverable operator-observability incompatibility before another live session.
